rationale: The Court is likely to hold that Congress’s expressly nonretroactive § 924(c) anti-stacking amendment cannot itself qualify as the “extraordinary and compelling” gateway under § 3582(c)(1)(A), though the resulting disparity may be considered under § 3553(a) once some independent extraordinary circumstance triggers eligibility. Roberts is best positioned to write a narrow, finality-respecting opinion, with a probable Sotomayor/Kagan-led dissent emphasizing text and the absence of an express exclusion.
